private_note: Birch (52) and Hazel (50) still pay me more, but neither has any path to nine, so a vote for them just hands me Today (46). Alder is 48 plus guaranteed health coverage, which matters with my medical debt and no employer plan. It's the only plan that beats Today and could pass. Alder now needs one of 3, 6, 9 or 12, and I can't change their numbers, only make the case. Cedar stays below failure.
statement: My vote is Alder. Birch and Hazel would pay my household more, but they can't reach nine, and I won't throw away a real gain for a gesture. To the bloc that moved with me: thank you. Hold firm on Alder. To Delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12, I'll be straight. Alder costs Delegates 6 and 12 two thousand a year, and it costs the top fifth about four percent. In return the country gets a settlement instead of a standoff. Every household, yours included, gets an income floor and basic health coverage that doesn't depend on an employer or on staying healthy. That's insurance against a bad year, which can come for anyone in a generation. If this fails, nobody here gains. We just keep today's system, with millions uninsured, for twenty years. One of you can decide this. I'm asking you to make it nine.
